style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: Matte clay 3D render of two small mechanical assemblies side by side on a concrete basement floor: left, a rounded steel heating-oil tank with a fill pipe and analog pressure dial (no markings); right, a rectangular heat-pump condenser unit with louvered grille and coiled copper lineset. Split-screen diptych with left-right contrast. A single hard directional key light from the left rakes across both assemblies, casting long contact shadows. Muted palette of slate grey, rust, and deep pine green. Matte surfaces with moulding seams. No text, no logos, no lettering, no numbers.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, embossed lettering, printed markings, UI elements
rationale: The story is a structural policy and cost dilemma—staying on expensive oil versus paying more to leave it. A matte 3D clay render with two recognizable household heating components in a split-screen diptych states the contrast without legible text, avoiding the lettering that failed the previous frame.
subject: A residential heating-oil tank with analog gauge beside a heat-pump condenser unit on a concrete basement floor
core_thesis: Heating oil hit $6.19 a gallon in October while the federal reserve release covers about a day of demand and install materials rose 3-15% — the fuel is a record and the exit from it got dearer.
core_conflict: The federal reserve loan of 315,000 barrels is tiny against a daily burn of 262,000 barrels, while the cost of staying on oil is at a record and the cost of switching to a heat pump also jumped 3-15%.
composition: split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast

review.depicts: A split-screen image with a grey-green horizontal heating-oil tank topped by a round analog gauge and a bent fill pipe on the left, and a grey-green heat-pump condenser cabinet with a louvered grille and coiled copper tubing on the right, both sitting on a cracked concrete floor under hard light.
review.reason: The diptych literally stages the article's subject — the oil tank in the $6.19-a-gallon heating story set against the heat-pump alternative whose installation costs are rising — rather than a stand-in from another industry.
